technical_summary: Purportedly AI-generated video ads using OPay branding and a synthetic voice were served through TikTok's advertising system to lure users into sharing account details, enabling social-engineering theft of an OTP and fraudulent betting-voucher transactions.

technical_summary: Front Assist and Audi pre-sense automatic emergency braking systems, which use sensors to detect obstacles and brake autonomously, were alleged to produce false activations. Four class actions were consolidated and settled without admission of defect.

summary: A Washington Post investigation found police departments across the US arresting people based on facial recognition matches without independent evidence, contrary to their own policies. At least eight people were wrongly arrested, including a man jailed for a crime he says he did not commit.
technical_summary: Police used facial recognition software that searches mugshot databases, even with poor-quality images, and treated candidate matches as sufficient grounds for arrest. Departments skipped corroboration required by internal policy, so false matches led to wrongful arrests.

notes: Mechanism is officers treating unverified matches as evidence; error also stems from match quality.

summary: In a newspaper test, Turnitin's new AI-writing detector flagged part of a high school student's original essay as likely written by ChatGPT. The reporter found the tool got more than half of 16 test samples at least partly wrong.
technical_summary: Turnitin's AI-writing detector assigns generated-by-AI scores and sentence-level analysis to student work. In a journalist's test it produced false positives on human-written text and misclassified several mixed or AI samples, with no way for teachers to compare to source documents.

notes: Harm was a false flag in a test, not a documented disciplinary outcome.

summary: Minutes after Kosovo's parliament elected a new speaker, a purportedly AI-generated Facebook video used his likeness to claim he was the father of the Ashkali community. It reportedly drew over 80,000 views in under eight hours.
technical_summary: A synthetic video using a politician's likeness and a fabricated statement was posted to Facebook immediately after a high-profile political event. Generative video tools enabled rapid production of a convincing fake that spread before fact-checkers could respond.

summary: The Dutch data protection authority fined Clearview AI about 30.5 million euros for building an illegal facial recognition database from billions of photos scraped from the internet without people's consent. Clearview disputes the decision.
technical_summary: Clearview automatically scraped billions of face images from the web and converted them into biometric templates to sell identification services to law enforcement and intelligence agencies, without consent or sufficient transparency, in breach of the GDPR according to the regulator.

summary: Lawyers at firms in litigation with Madison Square Garden Entertainment were turned away from venues, including a Girl Scout chaperone at Radio City Music Hall, after facial recognition identified them. The company said the exclusion policy covers attorneys pursuing active litigation against it.
technical_summary: Madison Square Garden Entertainment used facial recognition, matching venue entrants against profile photos from law firm websites, to enforce an attorney exclusion list. The system worked as designed but enabled automated identification and exclusion of people by employer.

summary: A study found that Facebook's ad delivery system charged different prices to reach users depending on their inferred political alignment. This made it harder for political campaigns to reach people with differing views and may reinforce polarization.
technical_summary: Researchers ran political ads on Facebook and measured delivery. The platform's relevance-optimizing delivery algorithm preferentially showed ads to users it estimated as most aligned, raising the cost of reaching others, especially for small budgets, with the effect hidden by performance reporting.

summary: Philip Morris International reportedly promoted a tool that generated first-person responses to an EU tobacco consultation. Investigators linked hundreds of submissions to it and said it steered users toward arguments against stricter rules.

Most selectable options argued against regulation, and generated texts added unselected arguments, simulating grassroots opposition.
